tasks.title: Full when no seats are left
tasks.description:
In `RideRow`, the span with the class `seats` reads `Full` when `ride.seatsLeft` is `0`, and otherwise the number and ` seats left`, like `14 seats left`.

A full ride's span also has the class `full` beside `seats`, which paints it red. Any other ride's span has only `seats`.

The check draws rides of its own, full and not full, and reads the span's words and classes.
nextSteps: Read "One or the other" in the lesson.
Decide which words the span shows, depending on `ride.seatsLeft`.
Decide its class the same way.
Look at the ten thirty on the screen.
hints: There are two outcomes for the words and two for the class, and the same question decides both.
The conditional operator, `a ? b : c`, is an expression, so it works inside the braces of the text and of `className`.
Something like `{ride.seatsLeft === 0 ? 'Full' : ...}` for the words and `className={ride.seatsLeft === 0 ? 'seats full' : 'seats'}`.

tasks.title: Step-free only where it is true
tasks.description:
Show the span with the class `step-free` only for a ride whose `stepFree` is `true`. For any other ride the span is not there at all: not empty, not hidden, left out.

The check draws a step-free ride and one that is not, and looks for the element and for the words.
nextSteps: Read "Something or nothing" in the lesson.
Find the step-free span in `RideRow`.
Make the whole span depend on `ride.stepFree`.
Check that the Foundry Belle's rows no longer say Step-free.
hints: This time one of the two outcomes is nothing at all.
React draws nothing for `false`, and `&&` gives back its left side when that side is false.

tasks.title: Wheelchair spaces only when there are some
tasks.description:
Show the span with the class `wheelchair`, reading for example `2 wheelchair spaces`, only when `ride.wheelchairSpaces` is more than `0`. With no spaces, the row shows nothing for it: no span, and no stray `0` either.

The check draws rides with and without spaces, and looks at everything in the row.
nextSteps: Read "The 0 that shows up" in the lesson.
Make the wheelchair span depend on the number of spaces.
Look at the ten thirty: is there a 0 left on its row?
Make the condition a real true or false.
hints: The number of spaces is a number, not true or false.
`&&` gives back its left side when that side is falsy, and React draws the number 0.

tasks.title: Say when there are no more rides
tasks.description:
When `rides` is empty, `RideList` shows a `

` with the class `empty` that reads `No more rides today`, in place of the list: no `

    `, empty or not. With rides, it draws the list as before, without the message. The check draws `RideList` with no rides and with two.
nextSteps: Read "Return early" in the lesson.
At the top of `RideList`, ask whether there are any rides.
Return the message when there are none.
Try it: empty the array in `rides.js` for a moment and look at the screen.
hints: A component is a function, and a function can return from more than one place.
Check the length of `rides` before the list is built, where an `if` is allowed.

tasks.title: A notice that is only there when there is one
tasks.description:
Below `RideList`, write a component called `Notice` and export it by name. It takes one prop, `text`: - with a text, it returns a `

` with the class `notice` holding the text - with an empty text or none, it draws nothing at all Then use `Notice` in `src/App.jsx`, between the heading and the rides section, with the `notice` from `rides.js` as its text. The check draws `Notice` with a text, with an empty text and with none, then changes `rides.js` and looks at the screen.
nextSteps: Read the end of "Return early" in the lesson.
Write `Notice` below `RideList`, with its `text` prop.
Return nothing at all when there is no text.
Import `notice` and `Notice` in `App.jsx`, and use them above the rides.
hints: An empty paragraph is still on the page. When there is nothing to say, the component should put nothing there.
A component can return a value React draws as nothing. Both an empty string and a missing prop are falsy.
`if (!text) return null`, then return the paragraph. In App: `<Notice text={notice} />`.
